key_insight: A 3D U-Net predicts full 36-component strain localization tensor fields in heterogeneous concrete, with network width and depth emerging as the key scaling controls.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate repeated mechanical-field calculations in computational homogenization and multiscale simulations while supporting varied macroscopic loadings.
method: Train on voxelized concrete mesostructures up to 256³ using localization tensors from an FFT-based linear elastic solver.
Optimize U-Net architecture to balance accuracy and speed; conventional channel doubling after downsampling proves suboptimal.
Use Maximum Mean Discrepancy on internal feature maps to flag out-of-distribution microstructures without reference solves.
evidence_signal: The final model achieves 1.118% mean absolute error on both validation and held-out test sets and approximately 8.7× faster inference than the FFT solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU.
watch_item: Transfer across aggregate volume fractions is demonstrated, but reliable generalization depends on training with diverse morphologies; unfamiliar microstructures warrant screening.
paper_title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
